Nothing logged yet, so I'll give you the general approach. The simplest way is to split it into two chunks with a short break — say, run 5 miles easy, walk a few minutes to settle your breathing, then run the second half. Or build in a mid-run surge: easy pace for half, pick it up for a mile or two in the middle, finish easy. Some people anchor it to landmarks — a certain intersection or mile marker where they switch gears.

What matters is that you stay in control of your effort. Easy runs stay easy; if you're doing a long run with tempo or threshold work in it, that gets its own structure so you're not scrambling to find the pace mid-run.

What kind of long run are you building, and how long are we talking?
